cells.A2: Updated 24 Oct 2026, on the founders' 24 Oct inputs. Savers put away ₹100 a day by UPI into mutual funds in their own name (80% equity, 20% debt); we earn fund fees and, as a loan marketplace, referral fees from lenders. 9 in 10 savers come online, pan-India; 1 in 10 through doorstep agents in NCR. The app never holds anyone's money. Assumes debits cost us ₹0 and a 0.75% equity fund fee, both still to be confirmed in writing (₹2 a weekly debit would cut a saver to about 0.39× at 5 years, a 0.5% fee to about 0.49×).

cells.A13: The main case is the median of the LTV/CAC Monte Carlo (v4 Monte Carlo). Two inputs are still uncertain: still saving at 12 months (Bachatt's 30-40%) and our share of the debt fund's fee. Everything else is fixed by the founders (market figures, Bachatt, or our judgement: ₹70k first loans, 20% apply and 20% approved, home ₹12 lakh and property ₹5 lakh, lender payout 2% flat, debits ₹0, no recharge, bills, FD or NPS; the full list is on v4 README). Cost to win: ₹450 at scale (the founders' figure; they call it 'fairly sorted') plus the 10% contingency = ₹495. The seed budgets ₹600 while the brand is new, and measures it. 0.3% of the 1,000 draws reach 1× at 5 years, holding everything else at the main case; 90% by 8 years. 8 in 10 draws: 0.60-0.93× at 5 years, 1.00-1.76× at 8. The company is not EBITDA positive by month 96 in any of the 1,000 draws. At market numbers this is a fund-fee business; loans are a small add-on.
cells.A14: What it takes (v4 Monte Carlo; not another plan): ₹130 a day alone, or 40.5% still saving at 12 months alone, takes a saver to 1× at 5 years; no single loan lever does. 2× needs ₹161 a day, 41% still saving, 29% applying for a loan a year and 26% of first loans approved; the company then turns EBITDA positive from month 68 on $5.1M. 3× needs ₹194 a day, 44% still saving, 34% applying and 29% approved (EBITDA positive from month 55, $4.0M). The four facts that decide it, all cheap to get: Bachatt's average daily amount; Bachatt's exact 12-month retention; the ₹0 debit cost in writing (BSE StAR MF or the fund houses); the fee on the fund the ₹100 goes into, in writing (0.64% blended or better: the model uses 80% equity at 0.75% and the rest in debt at 0.22%, and daily minimums of ~₹100 a scheme likely mean one hybrid fund).

cells.A15: Words: LTV/CAC = what a saver brings in over 5 or 8 years, less the cost of serving them, divided by what it costs to win them. EBITDA = operating profit before interest, tax and depreciation. KYC'd = identity-checked. SIP = a regular investment into a mutual fund (here daily). Mandate = the saver's standing instruction for the debit. The Monte Carlo = we ran the model 1,000 times, picking retention and the debt fund's fee at random within their ranges; the median is the middle run, and P10-P90 is the range 8 in 10 runs fall in. Money needed = the seed + the deepest cash hole (fees arrive 2 months late) + a ₹5 crore cash buffer, at ₹95 = $1; '+' = at least, as the company is still losing money at month 96.
